polityNote: Ottoman Empire — the first-level units (vilayets, independent sanjaks and the Şehremaneti of Istanbul) whose ground is Anatolia and Eastern Thrace, 1891-01-01 to 1907-12-31, as unions of the 1893 kazas traced by Amasyalı from R. Huber's 1899 map. The scope starts after the reorganisations of 1888 (irade of 1/13 March 1888: Hakkari into Van, Dersim into Mamuretülaziz, Bayburt into Erzincan, Şiran and Kelkit to Trabzon; Karesi vilayet dissolved, Biga and İzmit independent) and after the Garbikaraağaç transfer (c. 1889); it ends before the first post-1908 changes of first-level outlines (Bolu independent after 1908, Karesi 1909, Istanbul vilayet 4 August 1909). Change list: Cuinet (t. I 1892, t. III 1894, t. IV 1894–95: caza lists and dated notes), the salname-based lists of Güneş (Istanbul), Söylemez and Aktaş (Çorum 1894), Karlangıç (Cebel-i Bereket), TDV and tr.wikipedia (1909 sanjak/kaza tables). Changes moving only a nahiye across a first-level line are not exhaustively known; the one found (Kargı, 1894) is handled in `unresolved`. ① measured 2026-10-06 on the atoms: 91 of 109 kaza seats matched by name to Wikidata district coordinates lie inside their own kaza polygon and 104 inside their own vilayet's (median offset 0 km, 90th percentile 3.2 km, worst 12.7 km); the traced coast departs from today's by up to ~10–20 km, so 19.7 % of Trabzon's union, 21 % of Istanbul's, 11.7 % of Çatalca's and 6–8 % of the Marmara and Black Sea units lie outside today's Turkey (mostly sea), while Kars–Ardahan–Artvin–Iğdır (Russian 1878–1918) are absent. Union areas against the Statesman's Year-Book figures for 1900 (statoids): Hüdavendigâr 1.08, Konya 0.96, Adana 1.08, Ankara 1.12, Kastamonu 0.96, Sivas 1.04, Trabzon 0.76, Erzurum 1.18, Van 0.84, Bitlis 1.04, Mamuretülaziz 0.98, İzmit 1.08, Biga 1.11, Çatalca 1.32, Istanbul 0.97; against Cuinet's own figures Hüdavendigâr 1.04, Aydın 1.06, Konya 1.07, Trabzon 1.05, Ankara (23 kazas) 0.86, İzmit 0.73.
